goal: Build a versioned reviewer eval corpus from committed audit records: eligible historical review cases with revision identity, finding anchor and evidence, acceptance text, and disposition, where resolved counts only as a silver label, gold labels are human-confirmed, clean cases are included, and the newest cases form a holdout validation split. Gold-case selection uses a pre-screen built on the shared decision-model decide() at a newly registered A1 application point, with a committed project egress ceiling that admits only finding to clef.

acceptance.assertion: Meet S0 in docs/specs/review-verifier-eval.spec.md: an offline extractor run at a pinned commit yields a deterministic corpus (same input commit produces byte-identical corpus.jsonl); a case enters the gold pool only when its finding is review-sourced with non-null evidence and anchor, its review_round is present, its review revision identity is recoverable, and both git objects are reachable, and ineligible records are excluded with counts by reason; the corpus validates against its schema and separates disposition (silver label) from gold (confirmed_true / confirmed_false / unlabeled) as distinct fields; the README states in its first paragraph that resolved is a silver label only and documents the gold labelling protocol (first set: 30 cases labelled by Derek, at least 10 confirmed_false or clean); at least 10 clean revisions from done tasks with no request_rework are included; the split is by task recency with the newest 20 percent held out as the validation split and is stable across regeneration. Selection of the 30 gold cases is uncertainty-first under an offline pre-screen (scripts/review-eval/prescreen.ts) that calls the shared decide() at application point a1_review_finding_prescreen with each extracted finding's trigger, caller_chain, and violated fields: least-confident cases and cases whose lean disagrees with the silver disposition are labelled first, and the item 3 weight rule breaks remaining ties. The classifier output is recorded only in a selection log (case id, probabilities, model, threshold-set version, path used: model or weight_rule, selected or not, reason) and never becomes a label or corpus gold. Disabling the pre-screen, and every unavailable decide() result (egress_denied, credential_missing, provider_error), each reproduce the weight-rule selection exactly with the log naming weight_rule for every affected candidate. The selection log and README contain no credential or environment-variable value.

The code-owned registry (plugins/immune-brain/runtime/decision_model/thresholds.ts) registers a1_review_finding_prescreen with input_category finding, options likely_true, likely_false, uncertain, and threshold set a1/v0 with values null; the committed project config .imm/config.json declares decision_models.egress.clef = ["finding"] and no other egress kind or category, so resolving the repository's effective configuration with a user egress request of clef/finding yields effective egress clef = ["finding"] and every other provider kind empty, while a user request of clef/diff is dropped with egress_beyond_project_ceiling.
